key_insight: ALICE unifies complementary pathology expertise from vision-only, vision-language, and slide-level teachers into one general-purpose foundation model. Instead of relying on a single pretraining style, it learns from multiple expert backbones to better cover different tasks and scales in computational pathology.
problem_solved: Computational pathology foundation models are often fragmented: different pretraining objectives, data types, and spatial scales create separate models with complementary strengths but no single unified backbone. This paper addresses the need for one model that can absorb and combine these diverse sources of expertise.
method: Uses multi-stage agglomerative distillation to transfer knowledge from eight teacher models into a single backbone.
Sequentially distills expertise from vision-only, vision-language, and slide-level experts into dedicated modules.
Pretrains ALICE on a very large pathology dataset of 24,985,184 tiles to build a broad general-purpose foundation model.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in pathology, ALICE offers a more unified starting point that may reduce the need to maintain multiple specialized backbones. It can simplify downstream adaptation across tasks while retaining strengths from different expert model families.

paper_title: ALICE: Learning a General-Purpose Pathology Foundation Model from Vision, Vision-Language, and Slide-Level Experts
paper_authors: Jiawen Li, Tian Guan, Huijuan Shi, Xitong Ling, Mingxi Fu
